definitions.explanation: A dark surface for writing on with chalk, used in classrooms.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{黒板|こくばん}に{書|か}いた。
examples.english: The teacher wrote on the blackboard.

examples.japanese: {黒板|こくばん}を{消|け}してください。
{黒板|こくばん}の{字|じ}が{小|ちい}さくて{見|み}えない。
examples.english: The writing on the blackboard is too small to see.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{黒板|こくばん}に{問題|もんだい}を{書|か}いて、{生徒|せいと}に{答|こた}えさせた。
examples.english: The teacher wrote a problem on the blackboard and had the students answer it.

examples.japanese: {教室|きょうしつ}の{前|まえ}にある{黒板|こくばん}は{大|おお}きいから、{後|うし}ろの{席|せき}からでも{字|じ}がよく{見|み}える。
examples.english: The blackboard at the front of the classroom is large, so the writing is easy to see even from the back seats.

notes:
{黒板|こくばん} is a classroom blackboard.

RELATED ITEMS:
- チョーク (chalk)
- {黒板|こくばん}{消|け}し (blackboard eraser)
- {黒板|こくばん}{拭|ふ}き (blackboard cleaning cloth)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {黒板|こくばん}に{書|か}く (to write on the blackboard)
- {黒板|こくばん}を{消|け}す (to erase the blackboard)
- {黒板|こくばん}を{見|み}る (to look at the blackboard)

MODERN ALTERNATIVE:
- ホワイトボード (whiteboard)
- {電子|でんし}{黒板|こくばん} (electronic whiteboard)

NOTE: Despite the name ({黒|くろ} = black), modern school blackboards are often green.
